items.faults: Forced pick (hand retouch, ear drop removed). Remaining faults: (1) Nagoji's left ear is visible but now shows no gold stud at all; the retouch took out the stud along with the drop, so the bible's 'small gold ear stud' is missing. (2) Nagoji's chin has a faint stubble shadow. The bible allows 'light stubble at most, captivity only', and chapter 8 is after captivity. (3) He is barefoot with no boots, and his talwar leans against the tree. That suits sitting on the platform but differs from the commander sheet. (4) Padmini reads as perched on the platform edge with her weight on the stick, not clearly rising, so the 'getting to her feet' beat is weak. (5) Her head sits near the top edge, above the middle half of the frame. The open sky in the upper middle and right (x about 0.45 to 0.95, y 0.05 to 0.35, broken only by palm crowns) gives room for all three lettering lines. Nagoji's line can go above him in the sky, and Padmini's two lines to the right of her head, clear of the faces. No painted text, balloons, gore or anachronisms. Hands and anatomy are sound. Padmini's black hair, gold jewellery and cream gold-border sari with no blouse match her bible row.

Forced pick past the two-correction stopping rule (Claude, 2026-10-08). v04 is a hand retouch of v02 (see HAND-RETOUCH-2026-10-08.json): Padmini alone in the anteroom, on model, eyes on the middle distance, leaf lowered, clear wall for both balloons. The faint pseudo-text on the leaf is smoothed away. Remaining fault for the author: the leaf is a short, broad tag with a pale cord, not the long narrow ola strip with the red braided cord of 2.4.

Forced pick, with three faults left. (1) De Lannoy is seen from behind and the linen bandage is on his RIGHT wrist (viewer's right, by the guard's back). The bible puts it on the LEFT, and his bare left hand is visible at the viewer's left of the coat. v02 has the same fault. (2) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead sitting slightly below the lobe, not a flush stud. It is smaller than v02's clear stud-plus-drop, which is why v03 wins on this point. (3) Ramayyan wears a tiny gold ear stud, and he should have no jewellery. The rest matches the script beat. De Lannoy's back, in the torn blue coat with boots and pale hair, goes out the door between two bare-chested Nair spearmen. Nagoji stands aside by the wall: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, talwar, boots, thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. Ramayyan looks up from his leaf, and Varma, bare-headed with the side knot, namam and pearls and with his spear beside him, watches the door. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the bare upper granite wall between Nagoji and the window (about x 0.47 to 0.71, y 0 to 0.27) and the window sky. v01 is rejected: Varma has loose curly greying hair, Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up showing the brand, and De Lannoy wears a white skirt.
items.retouch_hint: A small local pixel retouch would fix all three faults. (a) Paint the white linen wrap off De Lannoy's RIGHT wrist and hand (about x 0.21 to 0.235, y 0.425 to 0.50), continuing the blue coat cuff and the skin of his hand. Then paint a matching narrow linen bandage round his bare LEFT wrist and hand (about x 0.09 to 0.12, y 0.47 to 0.52). (b) Shrink Nagoji's gold ear bead (about x 0.425, y 0.195) to a tiny flat stud flush on the lobe, with nothing below it. (c) Paint out the small gold stud on Ramayyan's earlobe (about x 0.64, y 0.518) in skin tone.

items.faults: Forced pick (past the two-correction rule; v04 is a hand retouch). Faults for the author: (1) Key beat only partly shown: Nagoji's hand does not close on Revathi's wrist. A male hand grips his own upper arm just below her bangled wrist, and its arm comes from behind his arm on her side. It is unclear whose hand it is: it reads as his far-side left hand reaching across, or as a stray third hand. His near (right) arm hangs straight down with the hand resting on his lap. (2) The lighting is too bright and warm for midnight with no lamp. Both faces and his torso are evenly lit as if by a lamp, not by the faint glow from the barred window with deep shadow around them. (3) A light stubble shadow on Nagoji's chin and jaw: minor, but the bible says clean-shaven, smooth skin. (4) Revathi's fingers already rest on top of his shoulder, not tracing up the arm past the bandage edge. Acceptable, but less of a 'tracing' motion. (5) Her hair is loose and curly around her face, softer than the neat sheet hairline. Her bell jhumka earrings match her sheet. Correct: Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a tiny flush gold stud, no grey, no turban, and a rib bandage plus a slipped shoulder cloth. Revathi has an indigo and gold sari, a jasmine braid, a flat-coin necklace, armlets and a sandalwood line, with no red dot. The room has a barred window, palms, a timber door and a mat, with no bed and no text. There is clear dark wall space for Nagoji's balloon above his head (about x 0.46 to 0.73, y 0.02 to 0.16) or on the wall right of his head below the window.

Forced pick (hand-retouched v04). Faults for the author: (1) Nagoji has a clear streak of grey hair at the temple below the turban, but on page 13 he should have no grey yet. (2) His ear stud is a round gold bead, a little larger and more prominent than the tiny flush stud, though nothing hangs from it. (3) There is faint stubble-like texture shading on his jaw and chin. It does not read as a beard, but it is not perfectly smooth. (4) Blue coats show up early. The page 13 beat is that the blue Company coats are only now being unfolded (13.4), yet a background officer at right wears a full blue coat with a red sash, the dais figures wear blue coats and caps, and every infantryman has a blue sash. (5) The background infantry wear white trousers and boots instead of dhotis and bare feet, which jars with page 14. (6) The background firing line aims roughly toward the left foreground, where the two principals stand. Fortunately it is distant and blurred. (7) The 'dais' at left is a tall two-storey timber stand with bearded onlookers, not a small timber dais. (8) The ship on the horizon is small and at anchor, so it is acceptable per 13.3. Good points: Lannoy matches his sheet (pale wavy hair with black ribbon, white high-collared tunic-coat, bare-headed, hands behind back), the cupped-hand whisper beat is clear, and the brand and scar sit on the raised inner LEFT forearm. There is no painted text, and anatomy is sound. Lettering space: clear sky at the upper centre-left above Nagoji's turban (about x 0.28-0.45, y 0.0-0.09) and a broad clear sky band at upper right (x 0.62-1.0, y 0.0-0.24). Tails run to Nagoji's mouth behind his cupped hand.

Forced pick (v04 hand retouch); faults for the author: (1) Nagoji's temple grey reads as a clear silver streak above the ear, stronger than the 'faint grey' the bible asks for on page 19. (2) Nagoji's chin and jaw carry a faint grey-brown shading that reads as shading at print size, but it could pass for light stubble on close inspection. Moustache is thick and curled, and the small gold stud on the lobe is correct. (3) Nagoji's sword is near-straight with a stirrup knuckle-guard and a brass chape, closer to a European hanger or sabre than a curved talwar. (4) The guardroom door stands open onto a moonlit battlement exterior. The script only places Nagoji by the door, so this is acceptable, but the room is less enclosed than the prompt's low timber door implies. (5) Ramayyan's face is heavier and older than his sheet, though the receding hairline, curly side hair, plain white cloth, palm leaves and stylus all match, with no forehead marks or thread. (6) There is a corner clutter of staffs or musket-like poles, a pot and a spear rack. It is period-plausible but busy. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, both hands turning the chipped stone, standing apart. The clay lamp has an open wick. No painted text, balloons, blood or noose. Hands are sound. The clear upper wall from about x 0.30 to 0.75 and y 0.02 to 0.30 holds all three balloons. Ramayyan's two balloons go above him (centre top), and Lannoy's short line sits upper right, left of his head.

FORCED PICK, least bad of three. v01 is out: only two men are drawn and Nagoji is missing. Why v03: both principals match their sheets and the page. Varma is bare-headed with sleek black hair in a knot (matching 5.1), a pearl drop earring, one gold chain, a cream mundu, no crest and no spear. Nagoji has a high topknot with grey temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold stud and the silver chain with its medallion (matching 5.3). The setting is right: sanctum and lingam at screen left, jackfruit tree at right, niche lamps, night. The blade points at Varma's throat and he lunges forward into it, palm against the chaver's fist, so he is stepping in. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Remaining faults for the author: (1) The chaver is wrong and does not match 5.2 to 5.4. He has a MOUSTACHE (the script says clean-shaven) and a shaved head with a small tuft at the nape, where the neighbouring panels show black curly hair. He also wears a rudraksha bead string. The ochre torn tunic, red sash and ash stripes do match. (2) Nagoji has both hands on the chaver's FREE (non-dagger) arm, near the elbow. The script and 6.1 need his LEFT hand still dragging on the DAGGER wrist. The dagger arm is held only by Varma's palm. (3) Nagoji's arms are crossed and hard to read. Rough brand or scar texture shows on BOTH forearms, but the brand belongs only on the inner LEFT forearm. (4) Varma's free hand is a loose fist at his chest, which is fine. No lettering lines, so no tails. Why v02 is only the backup: its beat is better (Nagoji grips the dagger arm itself) and its chaver matches the neighbours (curly hair, clean-shaven, ash stripes, ochre tunic, red sash). But Varma has long loose curly hair with a crown bun, which matches neither his sheet nor 5.1. And Nagoji's forearm brand is painted as dark glyph-like marks that read as pseudo-letters.
items.retouch_hint: Small local retouch, two spots. The moustache on the chaver's upper lip at about x 0.513 to 0.527 and y 0.215 to 0.227 of the frame: paint it out with the surrounding skin tone so he is clean-shaven. Optionally, the rough brand or scar texture on Nagoji's upper forearm (his right arm, the one crossing higher) at about x 0.70 to 0.75 and y 0.26 to 0.30: soften it to plain skin so the brand shows only on the lower (left) forearm near x 0.79 to 0.85, y 0.36 to 0.38. The chaver's shaved head and Nagoji gripping the wrong arm cannot be fixed by retouch. If v02 is used instead, retouch its forearm brand at about x 0.70 to 0.76 and y 0.43 to 0.49, painting the dark glyph-like marks into a pale puckered scar patch with no letter shapes. Varma's loose curly hair in v02 is not locally fixable.

items.faults: Forced pick, least bad of three. v03 gets the beat right. The chaver (clean-shaven, ash-striped brow) has the dagger raised toward Varma, so Varma is inside its arc. Varma's right hand drives stiff-fingered into the chaver's throat. Varma matches his sheet: sleek black hair in a knot, pearl drop earring, one gold bead chain, bare-chested, cream mundu, no crest and no spear. Nagoji is at the right edge with a topknot, grey temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small ear stud and a silver chain. The courtyard (jasmine doorway, lamp niches, peeling wall, jackfruit tree, night sky) is correct, and there is clear dark sky top-centre for the caption. Remaining faults: (1) Nagoji grips the chaver's forearm with his outstretched RIGHT arm, not his LEFT hand. That arm also carries the brand and white scar, which repeat correctly on his left forearm (the lowered arm at screen right), so the scar appears twice. (2) The hands on the dagger arm are a tangle. Varma's left arm ends in a fist under the knot of hands instead of clearly clamping the forearm, and the chaver appears to grip his own dagger wrist with his other hand. At print size it reads as several hands holding the blade back, not as Varma clamping above Nagoji's lock. (3) Nagoji's grip sits near the chaver's elbow rather than on the wrist. (4) Varma's forehead has ash stripes and a red dot. That is acceptable, since 6.2 needs sandal paste to smear, but the mark is not the sheet's exact namam. Rejected alternatives: v02 puts the dagger in VARMA's left fist, attached to his own arm, so the king seems to be stabbing an unarmed chaver. v02's Varma also has loose curly hair unlike his sheet. v01 has no chaver at all: Varma is choking Nagoji.
items.retouch_hint: A small local retouch fixes the worst visible fault in v03. Paint out the duplicate brand (circular tattoo-like mark) and pale diagonal scar on Nagoji's outstretched gripping forearm, roughly x 0.61 to 0.69 and y 0.58 to 0.64 of the frame, with plain skin tone. Keep the scar and brand on his lowered forearm at screen right (about x 0.85 to 0.92, y 0.68 to 0.74). The wrong gripping hand and the tangle of hands on the dagger arm cannot be fixed by retouching.

items.faults: FORCED PICK (least bad). v02 shows the right three figures and the beat reads: Varma pins the clean-shaven chaver (ash-striped brow, eyes on the steel). Nagoji is up on one knee on the right with the dagger raised, and he matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, high topknot with grey at the temple, silver chain. The courtyard (sanctum with lingam and jasmine at left, niche lamps, jackfruit roots at right, night) and the light match the setting. There is no painted text, no blood and no balloons. The two captions fit in the sky and upper wall across the top (roughly x 0.30 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17, plus the band over the shrine roof at top left), clear of every face and of the dagger hand at about (0.30, 0.20). Remaining faults for the author: (1) HAND SWAP. Nagoji holds the dagger in his RIGHT hand, while his LEFT arm, which carries the brand/scar, hangs at his side. The script wants the dagger in the LEFT hand with the right arm hanging useless. At print size this reads as 'the arm hanging' but is wrong in the details, and the 8.4 insert (dagger in the branded left hand) will not match it. (2) The chaver lies flat on his back. He is not arched with his chest thrust up at the point, and the dagger tip aims at his brow and eye rather than his chest. (3) Varma has bushy curly hair with a bun on the crown. That is closer to Nagoji's hair than to the sheet's sleek hair with a side knot above the left ear, so the two men look a little alike. Pearl earring and gold bead chain are correct. (4) Varma bears down with his arms and chest rather than his RIGHT shoulder. Rejected v01: the chaver is missing, and Nagoji (silver chain with medallion, topknot) lies pinned under Varma in the chaver's place, so the beat is lost. Backup v03 has the same hand swap and also a second, prominent pink brand on Nagoji's raised RIGHT forearm (a doubled brand). Its Varma is closer to his sheet (sleeker hair, forehead mark).

Forced pick (least bad). v03 has the best likenesses on the page: Nagoji with a thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold ear stud, high topknot with grey temples, silver chain and the brand on the inner LEFT forearm; Varma with sleek black hair in a side knot, namam, pearl earring, moustache and one gold chain, no crest and no spear. It also matches the pick for 9.3 exactly. The old priest holds the heir behind the pillar, the dog lies against the far wall, the body lies face down in a plain white mundu with no red and no blood, and the scene has the high angle through the jackfruit canopy. There is plain wall space at upper centre (x 0.35 to 0.57, y 0.05 to 0.28) and to the right of the door for the two captions. Remaining faults: (1) the worst one: Nagoji holds the dagger in his RIGHT hand, the arm that should hang useless, not lowered in his left and held away from his body, which breaks continuity with 8.2 to 8.4; (2) Nagoji wears a cream shoulder cloth that is absent in 9.3 v03 (minor); (3) the lingam in the sanctum carries a white U mark rather than ash stripes (minor, tiny at print size). Rejected alternatives: v02 has the dagger in the correct left hand, but Varma has a loose curly mane with no side knot and looks too much like Nagoji, a red waist cloth spreads under the body and could read as a pool of blood, and Nagoji's right hand is planted on the floor. v01 draws Varma with no moustache (fails his sheet), puts a red mark on Nagoji's forehead and gives the body a red sash.
items.retouch_hint: Yes, a local retouch would fix the worst fault. On v03, paint out the dagger (hilt and blade) in Nagoji's right hand at about x 0.285 to 0.305, y 0.66 to 0.745 of the frame, and continue the stone step and floor behind it, so his right hand hangs empty. If the dagger must stay in the panel, clone that same dagger into his left hand, which rests on his left thigh at about x 0.44 to 0.46, y 0.63 to 0.70, with the point turned down and slightly away from his body. Optional: tint the white U mark on the sanctum lingam (about x 0.045 to 0.06, y 0.21 to 0.25) to grey ash stripes.

items.faults: Forced pick (least bad). v03 shows the beat. On the left, Varma eases himself up off the chaver's body, his hands on the man's back and on the stone. He matches his sheet: sleek black hair in a side knot, namam with a thin cut across the brow, pearl earring, moustache, one gold bead chain, bare chest, cream mundu, no crest and no spear. On the right, Nagoji rises on one knee, his left fist clenched at his chest and his right arm hanging. He matches too: thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold ear stud, high topknot with grey temples and silver chain. The dagger lies on the stones by the chaver's hand. There is no blood, the courtyard (shrine at left, jackfruit at right) matches 9.1 v03, and dark night sky at top centre (x 0.40 to 0.72, y 0.0 to 0.15) plus wall below it give room for both balloons. Remaining faults: (1) a brand-like scar line and raised marks also appear on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm (image-left forearm), duplicating the left-forearm brand; (2) the split, swollen lip and the lower right shoulder that the script asks for on Varma barely read; (3) Nagoji's 'left hand clenched over the cut palm' reads only as a fist at the chest. Rejected alternatives: v02 lays the body on a red-and-yellow striped cloth that is not in the setting, puts the dagger back in the dead chaver's hand (contradicting 9.1) and gives Varma a loose curly mane with no side knot. v01 leaves out the chaver's body altogether and has red marks on Varma's lip and Nagoji's hand that read as blood.
items.retouch_hint: Yes, a small local retouch would fix the worst fault. On v03, remove the white scar line and the raised brand marks from Nagoji's RIGHT forearm (the forearm at screen left of his figure, about x 0.607 to 0.634, y 0.475 to 0.625 of the frame) by repainting it as plain, unmarked skin to match the surrounding arm. Leave the brand on his left forearm (about x 0.80 to 0.86, y 0.50 to 0.54) untouched.

items.faults: FORCED PICK. All three candidates show Varma toasting with his RIGHT hand, the arm under the cream cloth on his injured shoulder. The script asks for both men to toast left-handed, so this fault is in every candidate. v03 is still clearly the least bad. Varma matches his sheet: sleek hair, side knot over the left ear, pearl drops, gold beads, stitched brow, and a wincing half-laugh. Nagoji is correct: topknot, grey temples, flush stud, clean chin, silver chain with pendant, right arm in a sling, and his wrapped left hand meeting the cup with the unlettered brand on the inner left forearm. The cups meet over the lamp and the hands are sound. In v01 and v02 Varma has long curly hair and reads as a double of Nagoji. Other faults: the split lip is not visible, only implied by the wince. A few tiny grooms stand among the picketed horses in the courtyard. Lettering space: wall above Varma's head at upper left, the ceiling and doorway band at top centre, and the wall right of Nagoji's topknot at upper right.

v02 is the least-bad of the three. The beat works: the fingers stop just above a plain brass button on the white coat, which has a red waistcoat and lining. The face is softly out of focus behind the hand. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear studs, topknot, grey at the temples, silver chain. The room fits too: night war hall, open-wick brass lamps, latticed window, a map with plain lines. There is no text or pseudo-text, and the brand reads as scar tissue, not letters. Remaining faults: (1) The arm is mirrored. The reaching arm comes from his right shoulder, on the left of the frame, so the brand and scar are on the back of his RIGHT forearm. The script and bible put them on the inner LEFT wrist. (2) His shoulder cloth wraps both shoulders like a sleeveless vest, so his chest is covered. Panels 8.1, 8.2, 8.4 and 8.5 show it over one shoulder with the chest bare. This is a small costume mismatch. (3) The thumb is hidden under the hand. That is plausible but leaves only four fingers visible. Lettering: put the single NAGOJI balloon on the dark upper-right wall above the map (about x 0.65 to 0.95, y 0.03 to 0.20), clear of the face and hand. Why not the others: v03, the newest, has one arm with two hands (a second hand grows out of the top of the scarred forearm, which then carries on into a palm-up hand at bottom right). v01 has no coat at all; the finger touches a map counter, and his hair is long and loose with no topknot.
items.retouch_hint: No small local pixel retouch fixes the worst fault, the brand on the wrong arm. The art has no lettering, so a full horizontal flip of the frame is safe. The flip would make the reaching arm his LEFT arm and keep the face, coat and balloon space usable. The brand would still sit on the back of the forearm rather than the inner wrist. If the brand's side matters more than the composition, flip the frame. Otherwise accept it as is.
